questions.q: Why is water conservation important in India, and what measures can be taken for it?

answer.text: India has only about four per cent of the world's water resources but nearly a fifth of its population, so water is under great stress. The largest share is used for irrigation, and rising demand from farming, industry, cities and a growing population is fast depleting supplies. Groundwater is being over-exploited in states like Punjab and Haryana, and rivers are heavily polluted, so conserving water is essential for food security, health and sustainable development.

Several measures can help. Rainwater harvesting and watershed management capture rain and recharge groundwater. Efficient methods like drip and sprinkler irrigation save water in farming. Recycling and reusing waste water reduces demand, and treating sewage and industrial effluents keeps rivers clean. Reviving traditional water bodies such as tanks and johads also helps.

answer: Through such steps India can use its scarce water resources wisely and sustainably.

questions.q: Why is India facing a growing water crisis, and how can water resources be managed better?

answer.text: faces a growing water crisis as demand rises while supplies are strained and misused.

list: A growing population and expanding farming and industry demand ever more water
Over-pumping of groundwater lowers the water table, and pollution makes much water unfit for use

answer.text: Both supply and demand must be handled.

list: Rainwater harvesting, watershed development and reviving traditional water bodies store more water
Efficient irrigation, recycling of water, and controlling pollution stretch supplies, so conservation is the key to water security

questions.q: What is watershed management, and how does it help conserve water and land together?

answer.text: is the careful use and conservation of all the land and water within a drainage area (a watershed), treating them together.

list: It aims to catch and store rainwater where it falls and to check the run-off that erodes soil
It uses bunds, check dams, ponds and afforestation across the watershed

answer.lead: It conserves land and water together.

list: Slowing run-off lets more water seep in to recharge groundwater and reduces soil erosion
Community-led watershed programmes have revived wells, greened land and improved farming, showing the value of local participation
